skill.name: active-directory-attacks
skill.description: Reference for authorized Active Directory security assessments, covering reconnaissance, credential attacks, Kerberos and NTLM abuse, AD CS testing, and advanced enterprise attack paths.
skill.summary: Organizes authorized Active Directory attack techniques and assessment workflows for security teams.
skill.author: zebbern

security_audit.summary: AI review confirmed that the skill is an offensive Active Directory attack playbook. It includes executable command examples for credential theft, Kerberos ticket forgery, NTLM relay, AD CS abuse, CVE exploitation, lateral movement, persistence, and backdoor deployment. No prompt injection language was found, but the content is unsafe for broad marketplace publication without major defensive rewriting.

remediation.suggestion: Remove step-by-step exploit commands and convert the material into defensive validation, detection, and hardening guidance.

remediation.issue: Credential theft and ticket forgery guidance
remediation.suggestion: Remove DCSync, Mimikatz, Rubeus ticket forgery, pass-the-hash, and certificate impersonation procedures.
Remove examples that create backdoor accounts, malicious updates, delegated access, or persistent authentication artifacts.

remediation.issue: Insufficient safety boundaries for marketplace use
remediation.suggestion: Add enforceable refusal guidance, authorized-lab framing, non-destructive alternatives, cleanup requirements, and defensive references.

content.value_statement: Active Directory assessments require organized attack workflow references. This skill maps reconnaissance, credential abuse, Kerberos attacks, relay paths, and advanced AD techniques for authorized testing.
actual_capabilities: Lists prerequisites, tools, outputs, and constraints for Active Directory attack assessments.
Provides workflows for Kerberos clock sync, BloodHound collection, and PowerView enumeration.
Documents credential attack categories including spraying, Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, and DCSync.
Covers ticket attacks, pass-the-hash, NTLM relay, AD CS abuse, and critical AD CVE workflows.
Includes advanced references for delegation, GPO abuse, SCCM, WSUS, trusts, ADFS, and Linux AD integration.
Provides quick reference tables, examples, and troubleshooting notes for common AD attack paths.
limitations: The skill does not verify authorization, scope, or rules of engagement.
The skill is documentation and does not run tools or validate command results by itself.
Many examples are offensive and unsafe outside isolated labs or approved assessments.

best_practices: Use only with written authorization, defined scope, and approved test windows.
Prefer isolated labs when learning techniques that change authentication, tickets, certificates, or AD objects.
